findings.title: At the recommended 0.40 floor, the 1.08 area level comes from errors cancelling, which the registered flag cannot detect; the floor removes about 21 points of recall on human-mapped boulders at every size
findings.location: scripts/config_study.py:309-323 (count_ratio, mean_area_ratio, compensating); docs/configuration_study_plan.md:136 ('The compensating-errors flag is clear'), :145-147 ('at 0.40 the count ratio is 1.06x'), :229-230 (D36: 'discards about half ... likely including real boulders below the humans' mapping floor')
findings.detail: The flag is coded exactly as registered: pooled area ratio = (sum n_pred / sum n_true) x mean-area ratio. But missed human boulders and unmatched predictions both sit inside the count ratio and cancel there, so this test cannot see the main compensation at 0.40. I matched each detection to at most one human boulder on the 10 held-out tiles (C1, both sides >= 1.4105 m). The level of 1.08 at 0.40 breaks down as: about 30% of human boulder area with no surviving detection, offset by unmatched predictions (about +26%) and inflated masks on matched boulders (+12%). The recall loss is not confined to small boulders, and its size by image is what produces the 0.31x on ESP_025650_2165. So 'flag clear' plus 'count ratio 1.06' reads as 'the floor removes the false excess', but the floor also removes about a fifth of human-confirmed boulders of every size. That matters for D36, which the write-up calls the decision that matters, and for D13's SFD rollover.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the registered flag result as is, but add the per-boulder decomposition to the Results section and to the hirise2ctx brief. Say that the 1.08 at 0.40 is about -30% missed human area plus +26% unmatched detections plus +12% mask inflation, and that the balance varies by scene, which explains the per-image spread. Restate D36's cost as: held-out recall of human-mapped boulders >= 1.41 m falls from 0.89 to 0.68 at all sizes, including >= 6 m. Tell hirise2ctx that completeness at 0.40 is about 0.7 even for large boulders, which bears on D13.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
Held-out C1, IoU >= 0.3 one-to-one matching, both sides >= 1.4105 m:
- At 0.40: count recall 0.68, area recall 0.69, area ratio 1.08. Decomposition: missed -0.31, unmatched +0.27, inflation +0.12.
- At 0.10: count recall 0.88, area recall 0.89, area ratio 1.95. Decomposition: missed -0.11, unmatched +0.93, inflation +0.14.
- Recall by human size, 0.10 -> 0.40: 0.80->0.57, 0.92->0.72, 0.92->0.71 and 0.84->0.68 for 1.41-2.5, 2.5-4, 4-6 and >=6 m.
The registered flag's inputs stay as they are: count 1.063 and mean area 1.015.

Keep the registered flag (false, count 1.063 x mean area 1.015), and report next to it a per-boulder decomposition of C1 at 0.40, held-out:
- Human-boulder recall about 0.69 (vs 0.89 at 0.10), roughly uniform across sizes, including about 0.69-0.71 at 6 m and up.
- Human area covered by predictions about 0.64.
- The 1.08 level is the net of about -30% missed human area against about +26% unmatched and about +12% mask inflation (IoU matching; coverage-based measures give a larger offset).
- Per-image coverage at 0.40: 0.15, 0.60, 0.65, 0.70.
- State the D36 cost as a recall loss on human-confirmed boulders at all sizes, and tell hirise2ctx that completeness at the 0.40 floor is about 0.7 for D13.

findings.title: The held-out evidence comes mostly from the 0.5-0.6 m/px images; the '0.25 m/px tiles only' check is mostly training ground; on the 4 held-out 0.25 m/px tiles C1 is not tied with C1GS
findings.location: scripts/config_study.py:247-248 and :296 (subset 'res_025' keeps every split); docs/configuration_study_plan.md:66, :134-135 ('All six checks agree ... and the 0.25 m/px images alone'), :217-218 ('SAM2 adds nothing these 10 held-out tiles can measure')
findings.detail: RMSE pools cells, so the deciding 40 m statistic is weighted 88% by ESP_017355_2260 (0.5 m/px) and ESP_037018_2170 (0.595 m/px). The campaign runs at 0.25 m/px. The registered '0.25 m/px tiles only' check uses all 20 tiles of the two 0.25 m/px images, 16 of which trained the detector and YOLO's masks; that ground is optimistic and may favour the YOLO-mask candidates. Restricted to the 4 held-out 0.25 m/px tiles, the registered set still ties (C1 against best C1G: [0.81, 1.52]). The post-hoc C1GS separates, though: C1's RMSE / best is [1.06, 1.65], not tied, so the rule would not return C1 there. It does mean the claim that SAM2 adds nothing measurable once the floor is tuned is established only on the pooled, mostly coarse-resolution set. findings.title: 'Each 0.87x as large on average' is a population mean; matched YOLO masks are about 1.15x the human outline
findings.detail: The arithmetic checks out: the distinct-polygon count ratio (2.250) matches the cell-touch sum (2.234), and the union-vs-sum overlap loss is under 1.4%. But 0.87 is the mean area over all polygons, pulled down by about 1,900 small unmatched detections. Per matched boulder, YOLO masks are larger than the human outline. The headline 'mostly count' survives: unmatched predictions are about 0.90 of the 0.94 excess at 0.10, mask inflation about 0.13. Still, 'not mask size' / '0.87x as large' could be read by hirise2ctx as YOLO masks being smaller than human outlines. The PLAN_v3 factors (1.58-2.13x) cited at :32-33 were also withdrawn under BoulderNet G2-04.
findings.suggested_fix: In the brief, give the direct numbers: per matched boulder, YOLO is about 1.15x the human area (>= 1.41 m), worth about +0.13 of the +0.94 excess at 0.10; the rest is unmatched detections. Note that PLAN_v3's per-boulder factors were withdrawn (G2-04).

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
0.87 should be labelled as a population mean (all predicted polygons against all human polygons, held-out, at least 1.41 m, floor 0.10), not as a per-boulder factor. The direct numbers are:
- **Matched masks:** per IoU-matched boulder (n=1254), YOLO masks are 1.15× the human area (area-weighted; median 1.19) at 0.10, and 1.18× (n=966) at 0.40. The ratio is larger for small boulders: 1.36 at 1.41–2.5 m, 1.23 at 2.5–4 m, 1.09 at 4 m or more.
- **Excess at 0.10 (+0.94 of human area):** mask inflation on matched boulders about +0.13, unmatched detections about +0.92, missed humans about -0.11.
- **PLAN_v3 factors:** the per-boulder factors PLAN_v3 cites were withdrawn under G2-04 and should be flagged that way at lines 32-33.

findings.title: _mask_area_vs_yolo reports a median over every detection, unfiltered; on the label's population C1GS shrinks area by about 13%, not 20%
findings.detail: The matching is sound: 1 m centroid, optimal one-to-one, 99.4-99.6% of rows matched, and leaving out the two excluded dense tiles (8.7% of rows) changes nothing. But the statistic is a per-row median over all 50 tiles with no score or size floor, so small detections dominate it. The qualitative claim holds: C1G does not tighten at all, even area-weighted. The size of C1GS's tightening in label terms is about 0.87x rather than 0.80x.
findings.suggested_fix: Report the area-weighted label-population ratio (C1GS about 0.87x, C1G about 1.01x) next to the per-row median. Quote the area-weighted one in the brief.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: `_mask_area_vs_yolo` correctly returns the median of per-detection area ratios over all 50 tiles, with no score or size floor: C1G 0.974, C1GS 0.801. In the label's terms (area-weighted, registered 48 tiles, YOLO d >= 1.41 m, score >= 0.40) the ratios are C1G about 1.01x and C1GS about 0.87x (median 0.81). The difference comes from area weighting (large boulders shrink less, about 0.87 above 4 m), not from small detections dominating the median.

findings.title: 'Re-run config_study.py score' would not pick up a new size floor, and would overwrite the registered evidence
findings.detail: score() always uses le.STAGE4_MIN_DIAMETER_M: there is no CLI or size argument. It writes data/config_study/paired_cells.parquet in place, and that gitignored file is what posthoc (L399) and the size-floor sweep (scripts/review/config_study_size_floor.py:60) treat as the registered tile set. decide then overwrites data/review/config_study.json. If hirise2ctx moves the floor somewhere other than label_error.py, re-running score reproduces the 1.41 m result. If they do change label_error.py, the registered rows and JSON are replaced with nothing to distinguish them. config_study.json also records no BoulderNet code identity and no input or parquet hashes, unlike the other evidence JSONs.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a --min-diameter option with suffixed output paths, and record presets.code_identity() plus catalog and parquet hashes in config_study.json. Change the doc line to say how to re-run at a new floor without touching the registered files.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: `config_study.py score` always scores at label_error.STAGE4_MIN_DIAMETER_M. That is a constant hard-coded in hirise2ctx's label_error.py:67, separate from config_v2.yaml's `labeling.detection_filters.min_size_m`. A floor moved in config_v2.yaml is therefore not picked up. A re-run (score then decide) overwrites paired_cells.parquet, score_meta.json and config_study.json in place, and records neither the floor nor the BoulderNet code identity. To re-run at a different floor today you have to call paired(..., min_diameter_m=X) directly, as config_study_size_floor.py:68 does. Doc lines 181-182 should say so, or the harness should get a --min-diameter option with suffixed outputs.

findings.title: C1G/C3 re-masked 99.3% of rows below SAM's validated 1.0 logit px per native px; 'growth 1.0' does not cap the window
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md line 45 (C1G row: 'window 256, growth 1.0, as C3') and §Open lines 234-236 ('Its cause has not been investigated'); YOLOv8-BeyondEarth/src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/remask.py:130-146; scripts/render_rom_configs.py:14-17
findings.detail:
`max_window_growth` does not cap the window at 256 px.
- It only holds out a member whose own box span plus 2 × pad exceeds 256 px (remask.py:133-139).
- The window then grows to cover every remaining member's box ±16 px of pad (lines 143-146).
- At these densities almost every cell has a member near its edge, so almost every window is 273-315 px.

Measured from the per-row `logit_px_per_native_px` column:
- C1G: 443 of 58,812 rows at ≥1.0 (0.75%).
- C3: 409 of 58,243 rows at ≥1.0.
- Minimum 0.813, median 0.877. Validated G runs at exactly 1.0.

So the registered SAM2 candidates ran almost entirely outside the validated regime, not partly. The renderer's suggestion to 'restrict to 1.0' would keep <1% of rows. Backlog item 7 already records this for C3. The write-up's Open item, however, calls the 0.97× vs 0.80× gap uninvestigated without naming this measured, obvious first candidate. A reader of 'window 256, growth 1.0' would take it to mean the validated 256-px scale.
findings.suggested_fix: In the brief's note that config3/ is not validated SAM2, add: '99.3% of rows were re-masked at 0.81-0.94 logit px per native px (validated 1.0); max_window_growth=1.0 caps member span, not window size'. List it as the leading hypothesis for the 0.97× vs 0.80× gap under §Open.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
`max_window_growth=1.0` only holds out members whose own span plus 2×16 px exceeds 256 px. The window still grows past 256 px to cover every remaining member ±16 px. Measured on the rendered catalogs:
- C1G: 58,369 of 58,812 rows (99.25%) below 1.0 logit px per native px.
- C3: 57,834 of 58,243 rows (99.30%) below 1.0.
- Both: min 0.813, median 0.877, p90 0.938, max 1.049; window px median 292.
Validated in-slice G runs at exactly 1.0.

findings.title: C1GS does not drop SAM2 guard failures: they keep YOLO masks (726 rows, 1.2%), but several docstrings, and this audit's premise, say 'dropped'
findings.location: YOLOv8-BeyondEarth/scripts/render_rom_configs.py:195-196; src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/orientation_validation.py:1041-1043 and :1076; src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/remask.py:16-18; src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/predict.py:552-556 (contradicted by the code at predict.py:642-647)
findings.detail:
Since G2-03, a re-mask that fails a guard falls back to the detector's own mask, tagged mask_src='yolo' (predict.py:642-647).
- The C1GS manifests record 1,340 `remask_fallback_to_yolo` events before NMS.
- The C1GS catalogs hold 58,115 rows with mask_src='sam2' and 726 with 'yolo' (1.2%).
- render_rom_configs.py:195-196 nevertheless says these detections 'are dropped here, as the validated path does', and the sam2_remasker and remask.py docstrings say the same.

No number moves: on exact-score pairs the per-boulder C1GS/C1 area ratio is 0.801 on all pairs and 0.799 on sam2 rows only. But a brief that repeats 'drops guard failures' would mis-describe C1GS's detection content. C1GS keeps every detection that the edge, area and NMS steps keep.
findings.suggested_fix: Fix the four docstrings. In the brief, describe C1GS as 'SAM2 in-slice masks, with YOLO-mask fallback on guard failure (1.2% of rows)'.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: C1GS keeps every detection that survives the edge, area and NMS steps. When the SAM2 re-mask fails the background-grab guard or is degenerate, the detection keeps its YOLO mask with mask_src='yolo'. That happened 1,340 times before NMS and left 726 of 58,841 final rows (1.2%). C1GS should be described as 'SAM2 in-slice masks, with YOLO-mask fallback on guard failure (1.2% of rows)'. These stale docstrings should be corrected: render_rom_configs.py:195-196, orientation_validation.py:1041-1043 and :1076, remask.py:16-18, and the remask_fn paragraph at predict.py:552-556.

findings.title: C1GS manifests record no SAM checkpoint (null name/bytes/sha256 on all 50), so its provenance and config_hash cannot identify the SAM weights
findings.detail:
`sam2_remasker` takes the checkpoint from `sam_model.ckpt_path` or `sam_model.model_name`. Ultralytics' `SAM._load` overrides `Model._load` and never sets either, so both stay None from engine/model.py:114/119.

Every C1GS manifest therefore records:
- `remask_fn.config.checkpoint = {name: null, bytes: null, sha256: null}`
- `inputs.sam_checkpoint = {path: null, exists: false}`

Consequences:
- The config_hash cannot tell two SAM checkpoints apart. Review item A1's fix does nothing for real SAM objects, and the same gap applies to any production Solution-G catalog.
- That C1GS used sam2.1_b.pt is known only from render_rom_configs.py:60.
- C1G and C3 manifests do record sam2.1_b.pt (sha256 f1a9cf2dd69d…).
findings.suggested_fix: Let `sam2_remasker` take an explicit checkpoint path (render_rom_configs passes SAM_WEIGHTS) and hash it. Add a test with a real ultralytics SAM object. Until then, state in the brief that C1GS used sam2.1_b.pt (sha256 f1a9cf2d…) per the render script.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: The C1GS catalogs were made with data/weights/sam2.1_b.pt (161,935,802 bytes, sha256 f1a9cf2dd69d84bb463b5ad98246d03e2d47a130a9295db0ec967e6cd95e2e47), the same file C1G and C3 record. The manifests do not show this. The only record is the constant at render_rom_configs.py:60, and the call at line 215 passes no checkpoint path. `sam2_remasker` should take the checkpoint path explicitly, or read `sam_model.overrides`/its own argument, and hash it. It should not rely on `ckpt_path`/`model_name`, which ultralytics' `SAM._load` never sets.

findings.title: The study's 1.4105 m floor is Stage 4's configured value, measured in the image frame; the floor Stage 4 actually realises is 0.99-1.37 m
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md §'Cell size and size floor' lines 177-178 ('conditional on the 1.4105 m ... floor (hirise2ctx's current Stage 4 value)'); hirise2ctx src/label_error.py:249-251; src/labeling.py:108-114 and 436-442
findings.detail:
This is outside the inputs/renders scope, noted because the brief will discuss D13.
- Notebook 35, and so the harness, applies 1.4105 m to the equivalent diameter in each HiRISE image's own near-true-scale frame.
- Stage 4 applies it in the projected CTX frame, whose easting is stretched. hirise2ctx's own docstring gives the realised physical floor as 0.993-1.367 m over the 39 v2 images.
- So the study's cut is the configured floor, not the floor the labels were actually built at.

findings.title: Power is not stated where the tie is reported: 'tied' means a difference under ~15% is undetectable, and image-level variance doubles the SE
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md:134 ('Every candidate ties, so the simplest wins'), :225, :239-240
findings.detail: With 10 held-out tiles (about 3.7 effective), the paired tile bootstrap can only rule C1 out if it is about 15-17% worse than the best, at 80% power. The observed spread among the non-'score' candidates is 2.2% in the registered set and 5.5% with C1GS. So 'every candidate ties' was close to guaranteed once the floor absorbed the level, and simplest-wins then returns C1. The design is a non-inferiority test with a margin of about 15%. The tile bootstrap also treats tiles as exchangeable. Resampling images first and then tiles roughly doubles the SE, so the quoted CIs understate uncertainty for a new scene. That widens the ties and does not change the registered recommendation. The Open note ('not distinguishable at this sample size') is correct but sits far from the claims and gives no size.

Over the same ground the pooled area ratio cannot change with cell size, because the cells are nested and complete and fa is an area fraction. The 80 m and 160 m ratios (1.0834, 1.1004) equal those of their own 40 m children to about 1e-12. The 40 m held-out value of 1.0794 differs only in footprint. Coarse RMSE is the RMSE of child-mean errors: 0.0142 at 80 m, and 0.0113 at 160 m against 0.0263 at 40 m on the same footprint, a factor of 0.43 against the 0.25 of independent errors. No interval exists for the 160 m candidate comparison (12 cells, 6 tiles, 2 images).

findings.detail: Every held-out tile comes from one of the four scenes whose other tiles trained the detector. Even inside them, the share of detections a 0.40 floor keeps varies by scene and is lowest on exactly the two scenes that read low. That kept share can be measured on any scene without truth. findings.title: 'The compensating-errors flag is clear' hides that C1's 1.08 at 0.40 is a cancellation of misses against extras
findings.detail: The registered check multiplies an aggregate count ratio by an aggregate mean-area ratio (C1 at 0.40: 1.063 x 1.015). It therefore reads clear whenever misses and extras are similar in number and size. I matched C1 one-to-one against the human polygons on the same 10 held-out tiles: polygons >= 1.4105 m, centroid inside the complete 40 m cells, optimal assignment, IoU >= 0.3. The 1.08 turns out to be a net: area ratio 1.084 = 0.685 (share of human area matched) x 1.182 (matched-mask inflation) + 0.274 (unmatched detection area). So 31.5% of the human boulder area is missed (recall 0.679, precision against humans 0.641), and that gap is filled by unmatched detections and by masks ~18% too large. A centroid gate of max(r, 1 m) gives the same picture (0.702 x 1.168 + 0.264; 29.8% missed). On all 48 tiles: 1.016 = 0.724 x 1.146 + 0.187, with 27.6% missed. The plan frames this flag as the test for 'right for the wrong reason', so 'clear' reads as 'right for the right reason'. The level at 0.40 is not a per-boulder inventory. It holds only while extras roughly equal misses, and that is why it breaks per scene: ESP_025650_2165 has recall ~0.32 at 0.40 and an area ratio of 0.48 over its 10 tiles. The recommendation (C1) is not affected.
findings.suggested_fix: Keep the registered flag result and add one sentence: 'The level at 0.40 is a net. About 30% of the human boulder area is missed, offset by unmatched detections (~27% of it) and by matched masks ~1.18x too large. The registered count x mean-area test cannot see this, and the cancellation varies by scene.' Optionally report recall and precision against humans at each floor.

Held-out C1 at 0.40 decomposes as area ratio 1.08 = 0.69 (share of human area matched one-to-one, IoU>=0.3) x 1.18 (matched-mask inflation) + 0.27 (unmatched detection area, as a fraction of human area). That is ~31% of human boulder area missed, with recall 0.68 and precision 0.64 against humans. At IoU>=0.1 it is 0.71 x 1.18 + 0.25, 29% missed. On all 48 tiles it is 1.01 = 0.73 x 1.14 + 0.19, 27% missed. Held-out recall per image at 0.40 is 0.72, 0.17, 0.76 and 0.68 (ESP_017355_2260, ESP_025650_2165, ESP_028537_2270, ESP_037018_2170). Suggested addition: 'The level at 0.40 is a net. Roughly 30% of the human-mapped boulder area is unmatched, offset by unmatched detections (~0.2–0.27 of human area) and by matched masks ~1.15–1.18x larger. The registered count x mean-area check cannot see this, and the balance varies by scene.'

The registered flag result ("clear") stands as computed, but it should not be read as "right for the right reason". C1 at floor 0.40, held-out, 40 m cells, human polygons >= 1.4105 m with centroids in complete cells, one-to-one optimal matching at IoU >= 0.3: area ratio 1.084 = 0.685 x 1.182 + 0.274, with 31.5% of human area missed. Predicted-vs-human centroid offsets are 0.01-0.26 m on all four images, so registration does not bias the matching.

findings.title: Recommendation understates what the 0.40 floor removes: about a quarter of the detections that match human-mapped boulders, at every size
findings.detail: The doc says: 'It discards about half of the conf-0.10 detections, likely including real boulders below the humans' mapping floor.' The 'half' is right: 47.6% of in-cell polygons >= 1.41 m survive on held-out, and 47.7% of all C1 rows. But the floor also removes detections the humans confirm. On held-out tiles (IoU >= 0.3), matches fall from 1,104 to 848 (-23%), and recall against humans falls from 0.884 to 0.679. For human boulders >= 7 m, matches fall from 49 to 37 of 56. On all 48 tiles, matches fall from 5,621 to 4,367, and from 268 to 215 of 315 at >= 7 m. Missed human area rises from 11% to 31% on held-out. The doc's own size table shows 29% of detections >= 12 px dropped at 0.40, far above any mapping floor. This matters to hirise2ctx for the SFD and completeness work (D13) and for any count-based product built on a 0.40 catalog.

Matches fall 1104 -> 848, the >=7 m matches fall 49 -> 37 of 56, and missed human area rises from 11% to 31%. The 1.08 area ratio at 0.40 is therefore partly offsetting errors: misses are balanced by detections the humans did not map, which may be false detections or unmapped boulders."

findings.title: The 'not only a coarse-resolution effect' correction and 'not a small-boulder effect' go beyond the evidence: the excess sits at 6-10 px on every image
findings.detail: The correction argues that at 0.25 m/px the 1.41 m floor (5.6 px) is 'above the humans' roll-off', so ESP_028537_2270's 2.0x count ratio cannot be unmapped small boulders. But the 5.0 px human roll-off was measured on ESP_017355_2260's ROM tables and is described as 'matching its 5x5-px convention' (goal3_multiscale_fusion_plan.md:418). A 5x5 px square has an equivalent diameter of 5.64 px, so at 0.25 m/px the 1.41 m floor sits exactly on the mappers' minimum size, not on ground they demonstrably mapped completely. On ESP_028537_2270 itself (10 tiles, floor 0.10, IoU >= 0.3), human counts per px are flat from 6 to 10 px (315 in 6-8, 327 in 8-10, 390 over 10-14). The unmatched detections pile up in exactly that range. Unmatched/human is 2.38 at 6-8 px, 1.25 at 8-10, 0.56 at 10-14 and 0.18 at 14-20. In all, 1,159 of 1,531 unmatched detections (76%), and 54% of their area, lie at 6-10 px. Likewise, a 3 m size floor is only 6 px on ESP_017355_2260, the image carrying 92% of the held-out error, and that is still inside its excess band (6-8 px: 1,989 unmatched vs 1,172 humans). Notebook 35's own floor sweep shows the excess roughly halving by 5 m: the all-ROM 160 m ratio is 1.705 at 1.41 m, 1.657 at 3 m, 1.460 at 4 m and 1.348 at 5 m (held-out 1.948 -> 1.568). So the original caveat should stand at full strength: part of the excess may be boulders the humans did not map, and a floor fitted to human truth would then partly encode the mappers' completeness. That is exactly what D36 would be calibrating.

This truth cannot separate false detections from unmapped boulders, so a floor fitted to it may partly encode the mappers' completeness.' For the size floor: 'flat from 1 to 3 m; notebook 35 shows it falling beyond that (1.35x at 5 m).'

findings.title: The write-up rebuts PLAN_v3 numbers that BoulderNet's own G2-04 withdrew and hirise2ctx had already marked 'Unsupported'
findings.detail: The doc quotes PLAN_v3's 'YOLO masks are 1.58-2.13x the human area per boulder, SAM2's 1.06-1.27x' as the basis for the mask-area attribution, then says 'the results contradict it' and 'not supported by this decomposition'. BoulderNet's review G2-04 withdrew those factors (backlog:99: they 'compared a pixel count against a polygon area; they are not calibration factors'). hirise2ctx-pub DECISIONS 2026-10-14e already records 'Mask area is most of the 1.70x' as Unsupported for that reason. It also notes that because the count ratio (2.01x) exceeds the area ratio (1.70x), extra objects carry part of the bias. As written, the doc reads as BoulderNet overturning a hirise2ctx claim, when BoulderNet supplied those numbers and later withdrew them, and hirise2ctx's own correction is not credited.

Present the count-vs-area split as confirming their correction, and cite Test 3c (1.37x / 1.02x) as the valid per-boulder figure.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:

findings.title: The count x mean-area decomposition cannot test a per-boulder claim, and '0.87x as large' reads as YOLO masks being smaller than human ones (per matched boulder they are ~1.19x larger)
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md:145-147 ('each 0.87x as large on average ... not supported by this decomposition'); config_study.py:309-313 (mean_area_ratio = pooled_ratio / count_ratio)
findings.detail: 'mean_area_ratio' is pooled area over the summed per-cell touch count. It mixes per-rock mask size with the size distribution of the extra, mostly small, detections, so a value below 1 is fully compatible with masks larger than the human outline on every matched rock. That makes the stated argument invalid against a per-boulder claim. Placed next to PLAN_v3's per-boulder factors, '0.87x as large' implies YOLO outlines are smaller than human ones. I ran the proper same-convention test read-only: one-to-one matching, polygon against polygon, using the project's matched_area_ratio convention. It supports the conclusion more strongly than the decomposition does: at 0.10, matched-pair mask size explains only ~13% of the held-out excess (15% on all tiles), and unmatched objects explain ~87%. But per matched boulder C1's polygons are ~1.19x (median) the human outline, not 0.87x. The conclusion 'mostly count' survives; the evidence and the number given for it do not.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the decomposition sentence with the matched-pair evidence, along the lines of: 'per matched boulder (one-to-one, polygon vs polygon) C1's outlines are ~1.2x the human ones, which explains ~13% of the held-out excess at 0.10; ~87% is unmatched detections'. Drop 'each 0.87x as large', or label it explicitly as a population-mix statistic rather than a mask size. Optionally add the matched-pair readout to the harness so it is reproducible.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
Per matched boulder (one-to-one, polygon against polygon, size floor 1.4105 m), C1's outlines are larger than the human ones, not smaller:
- **Held-out, floor 0.10:** median 1.19×, IQR [1.03, 1.41], pooled 1.13×.
- **All tiles, floor 0.10:** median 1.18×, pooled 1.12×.
- **Excess at 0.10:** mask size on matched pairs explains about 13% of the held-out excess (15% on all tiles). Unmatched detections, net of missed humans, explain about 87% (85%).
- **Where 0.87× comes from:** pooled area divided by polygon count. It is a population-mix figure (pooled area ratio 1.94 over count ratio 2.25), not a mask size.
- **At floor 0.40:** matched masks still read about 1.2× (median), and the near-1 area ratio holds because about 32% of the humans go unmatched.

Matched one-to-one, polygon against polygon, C1's outlines are larger than the human ones. On the held-out tiles at 0.10: median 1.19x (IQR 1.03-1.41), pooled about 1.13-1.15x. Across all tiles: median 1.17-1.18x, pooled 1.12-1.14x. Mask size explains only about 13-15% of the held-out excess area at 0.10, and unmatched detections explain about 85-87%. The count ratio is 2.2x (unique 2.25, touch 2.23). Suggested wording: "per matched boulder C1's outlines are ~1.2x the human ones, explaining ~13-15% of the held-out excess at 0.10; ~85-87% is unmatched detections. So PLAN_v3's per-boulder 1.58-2.13x and 'mask area is most of the bias' are not reproduced." The 0.87x should be either removed or explicitly labelled as a mean over polygon populations, not a mask size.

findings.title: At the recommended 0.40 floor, a quarter of human-mapped boulders >=2.5 m lose every detection; the ~1.08 level is a net of misses and extras that the 'clear' compensating-errors flag cannot see
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md:134-136 ('The compensating-errors flag is clear'), :145-146 ('at 0.40 the count ratio is 1.06x'), :226-230 (D36 caveats: 'likely including real boulders below the humans' mapping floor')
findings.detail: The registered compensating-errors check is aggregate (count ratio vs mean-area ratio: 1.063 vs 1.015), so it passes. A matching-free spatial check shows real compensation at 0.40. Raising the floor from 0.10 to 0.40 removes every overlapping detection from about 20 points of the human-mapped boulders at every size, large ones included, not only boulders below the humans' mapping floor. The near-1 level comes from about a third of the human boulder area being missed and offset by predicted area that lies off every human outline (mask rings plus unmatched detections). By matched pairs, at 0.40 mask inflation (pooled 1.165x) is larger than the whole residual excess (143% of it). This matters for D36 (the decision the write-up calls the one that matters) and for D13/SFD use. It is also the mechanism behind the per-image spread: on ESP_025650_2165, 0.40 keeps only 15% of the human boulder area. 'Count ratio 1.06x at 0.40' is count parity, not the same boulders.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a third D36 caveat, for example: 'at 0.40 about a quarter of human-mapped boulders >=2.5 m have no kept detection on held-out ground; the label's level is the net of these misses against inflated masks and unmatched detections, a balance that varies by scene'. Qualify 'the compensating-errors flag is clear' as the registered aggregate check only. Consider reporting per-boulder recall against humans beside the area ratio at each floor.

findings.title: 1.4105 m is called 'hirise2ctx's current Stage 4 value', but v2's Stage 4 applies it in the CTX frame (realised 0.993-1.367 m); the harness applies it in the native frame, as v3 plans
findings.detail: The harness, like notebook 35, applies the floor to each polygon's own equivalent diameter in the native HiRISE frame, before clipping. v2's Stage 4 applies min_size_m after reprojection into the plate-carree CTX frame, so its realised physical floor is 0.993-1.367 m. The harness matches v3's planned rule (R2: apply the floor in the native frame), not current Stage 4. findings.title: The registered C3 is labelled 'configuration 3', but PLAN_v3's option 3 is '{512,256} + SAM2 re-mask (G)', and G-quality masks on the ladder were never tested

findings.title: The D9 recommendation covers only the label-quality leg of PLAN_v3's D9 pilot; whole-scene cost/RAM and D35's incidence pairs 'under every candidate configuration' are not covered
findings.detail: PLAN_v3's D9 rule is 'decide after a 2-3-scene calibration run that measures cost and re-runs notebook 35 for each configuration'. Choosing C1 on label quality alone is defensible, since it is cheapest and tied. But if hirise2ctx narrows to C1 first, D35's test cannot show an incidence x configuration interaction. findings.title: Resume deadlock: a later escalate run skips an arm that already completed with near-cap slices, and verify points the operator at a remedy that does nothing
findings.location: YOLOv8-BeyondEarth/scripts/run_multiscale_arms.py:199-217 (resume_point), :513-519 (skip on COMPLETE), :184-196 (attempt_key leaves out the mode); scripts/campaign.py:108-111 (verify message); src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/predict.py:241-243
findings.detail: Under on_max_det='error', a slice inside [0.9*cap, cap) does not stop the run. It is recorded as truncation {'slices_near_max_det': k}, the arm completes, and verify fails the scene with: 're-run detect, which escalates the cap'. Under the default escalate mode, resume_point returns the COMPLETE attempt (1100, 8) unchanged. Neither on_max_det nor the recorded truncation is part of the attempt key or the skip test, so ledger.status reports COMPLETE and the arm is skipped as 'up to date' on every resubmit. Verify then fails again, forever, until someone edits the ledger by hand. The same happens to an arm completed under --on-max-det warn, and to an escalate-mode arm that recorded nms_time_limit_batches. CAMPAIGN.md offers ON_MAX_DET=error as a supported mode ('restores fail-the-scene'), so this path is reachable from the runbook. It does not corrupt any output, because verify still blocks the truncated catalog.
findings.suggested_fix: In orchestrate, under escalate, do not accept a COMPLETE entry whose recorded truncation has slices_at_max_det or slices_near_max_det. Treat it as a max_det stop and continue at next_attempt(max_det, batch, 'max_det', ceiling). Alternatively, put the child mode into attempt_key. For the NMS-time-limit case, have verify name the real remedy (remove the arm's ledger entry and re-run, e.g. at a smaller batch) rather than 're-run detect'.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: Under escalate, orchestrate/resume_point should not accept a COMPLETE record whose recorded truncation has slices_at_max_det or slices_near_max_det. It should treat the record as a max_det stop and continue at next_attempt(max_det, batch, 'max_det', ceiling). An alternative is to put the child mode into attempt_key, so that an 'error'/'warn' completion cannot satisfy an escalate run. For the nms_time_limit case, verify's message should name the real remedy: clear the arm's ledger entry and re-run, for example at a smaller batch. It should not say 're-run detect'.

Under escalate, orchestrate/resume_point should not accept a COMPLETE entry whose recorded truncation has slices_at_max_det or slices_near_max_det > 0. It should treat that entry as a max_det stop and continue at next_attempt(max_det, batch, 'max_det', ceiling). An equivalent fix is to key the attempt on the child mode, or on the mode's stopping strictness. For nms_time_limit_batches, verify should name the real remedy (clear the arm's ledger entry and re-run, e.g. at a smaller batch), not 're-run detect'.

findings.title: Array ranges are 0-62, but hirise2ctx's v3 manifest has 62 rows (0-61): task 62 fails and its detect task pends forever
findings.detail: Every documented submission uses --array=0-62 or seq 0 62, which is 63 tasks. The manifest the campaign runs is v3_data/dataset/selection/manifest_v3.csv: 62 data rows (44 drawn + 6 anchors + 2 landers + 10 transfer), matching PLAN_v3:387 '= 62 BoulderNet scenes'. The '63' appears to be inherited from the older '~63 HiRISE' figure. Prep task 62 exits non-zero and sends a FAIL email. Detect task 62 (aftercorr) never becomes eligible and stays PENDING with DependencyNeverSatisfied unless cancelled, so the detect array never finishes cleanly. The DTN fetch loop ends on the same error.
findings.suggested_fix: Use --array=0-61 and seq 0 61. Better, derive the range from the manifest (e.g. a 'campaign.py count' subcommand) so a contingent swap cannot reintroduce the mismatch. Consider --kill-on-invalid-dep=yes on the detect array.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: The manifest has 62 data rows (0-61), so the ranges should be `--array=0-61%8` (prep), `--array=0-61` (detect) and `seq 0 61` (DTN fetch), in CAMPAIGN.md:51/57/66, campaign_prep.sbatch:15 and campaign_detect.sbatch:18-19. Better still, derive the range from the manifest row count, and pass `--kill-on-invalid-dep=yes` on the dependent detect array so a failed prep task cannot leave a stuck pending task.

findings.title: campaign_detect.sbatch adds an srun wrapper no proven job used; on Slurm 22.05-23.02 that step may be pinned to 1 CPU
findings.detail: CAMPAIGN.md says the cluster specifics are 'copied from jobs that have run (hirise_arms.sbatch, fuse_only.sbatch), per the standing lesson'. Those jobs call python directly (hirise_arms.sbatch:86). No sbatch that has run launches work through srun (the only other srun is an interactive nvidia-smi line in RUNBOOK.md). The srun line is new. Slurm 22.05 (late) through 23.02 stopped passing sbatch's --cpus-per-task to srun; 23.11 restored it. On those versions the single task can be bound to 1 CPU. It would then run the 8-thread mask-to-polygon pool, ultralytics' CPU preprocessing and GDAL decode on one core. Outputs are unchanged (worker count is order-preserving), but throughput drops, and an attempt is all-or-nothing against the 12 h limit. The stated reason for srun ('so sacct can report its MaxRSS') does not need it: sacct already reports the <jobid>.batch step's MaxRSS. GPU visibility is fine: steps inherit all of the job's GRES by default. Sherlock's Slurm version could not be checked from here.
findings.suggested_fix: Either drop srun (as in hirise_arms.sbatch) or use 'srun --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task="$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK"'. Have the pilot log len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) inside the step, and sinfo -V once.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: Either drop srun and call python directly, as hirise_arms.sbatch:86 does (sacct still reports MaxRSS for the .batch step), or use `srun --ntasks=1 --cpus-per-task="$SLURM_CPUS_PER_TASK" ...` (or export SRUN_CPUS_PER_TASK). Then correct CAMPAIGN.md:5-7, or note there that the srun line is new. For the pilot, run `sinfo -V` once and log len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) inside the step to confirm it has 8 CPUs. Separately, predict.py:1097 should size its worker pool from len(os.sched_getaffinity(0)) rather than os.cpu_count(), so a pinned step does not run 8 threads on one core.

findings.title: Host-RAM OOM-kill is treated as a crash and retried identically; --mem=64G is unmeasured at scene scale, and set -e skips the sacct line on exactly that failure
findings.detail: --mem=64G halves what the job that ran asked for (hirise_arms.sbatch, 128G). The only justification is N2's raster-side measurement. The detection-side term has never been measured on the cluster: the 2026-08-19 Sherlock arm manifests predate peak_rss_bytes, and the only post-N2 peak RSS is a 400-slice crop (1.95 GB at 5,518 detections). The pilot's scenes are larger: manifest_v3 gpx is median ~1.60, max 6.31 (3.3x ESP_017355_2260's 1.93 Gpx), at 0.25 m/px, where the detectable size floor halves. A cgroup OOM-kill reaches the orchestrator as returncode -9. That is not 3 or 4, so it raises CalledProcessError with no next_attempt. A resubmit resumes at the same attempt, re-runs the whole pass, and most likely dies again at the same end-of-run consolidation. The runbook has no entry for this case. Because srun's non-zero exit trips set -e, the sacct MaxRSS line, the diagnostic the pilot was meant to print, is skipped for exactly the failed task. Config 1 at 8 workers probably fits, so this is a risk rather than a demonstrated failure.
findings.suggested_fix: Include the 6.31 Gpx scene and the densest scene in the pilot. Add a runbook line: a step in state OUT_OF_MEMORY / exit -9 needs --mem raised on resubmit, because an identical resubmit dies the same way. Run sacct whether or not detect fails, e.g. 'srun ... || rc=$?; sacct ...; exit ${rc:-0}'.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
A host-RAM OOM kill (child returncode -9, or the orchestrator itself killed) is recorded as FAILED, or left as a bare 'running' marker, with no next_attempt. A resubmit then retries the identical (max_det, batch_size) at the same --mem=64G. No path raises memory, and the runbook gives no guidance for this case. When srun fails, set -e skips the sacct MaxRSS line for exactly that task. Fixes:
- Capture srun's rc, run sacct unconditionally, then exit with the rc.
- Add a runbook entry: OUT_OF_MEMORY / exit -9 means resubmit with a higher --mem.
- Include the 6.31 Gpx scene and the densest scene in the pilot.
The manifest gpx median is 1.54, not ~1.60. The max of 6.31 is correct.

findings.title: Escalation docs overstate it: the per-slice mask term grows with the cap, failed attempts are not reliably 'minutes', and an attempt longer than --time can never finish
findings.location: YOLOv8-BeyondEarth/scripts/run_multiscale_arms.py:38-40 and :160-161; sherlock/campaign_detect.sbatch:27-29; sherlock/CAMPAIGN.md:73, :75-76; docs/code_review_backlog.md 2026-10-14 handoff item 8
findings.detail: The docstrings, the sbatch header and backlog item 8 say that doubling the cap while halving the batch keeps 'the worst-case mask memory where it was'. Only the retained term (~1 MiB per detection x batch, cap x batch = 8,800 MiB) is constant. CAMPAIGN.md:84-86 itself says ultralytics holds ~5 MiB per detection of the current slice while building masks. That transient follows the cap alone: about 5.4, 10.7, 21.5 and 43 GiB worst case at caps 1100, 2200, 4400 and 8800. So on a 24 GB card, OOMs after escalation are expected, and the ladder will normally end in 'needs a larger card' rather than reach the model's 21,504 ceiling. Separately, 'each failed attempt stops at its first near-cap batch, usually in minutes' rests on a 25-slice ROM tile (7-10 s per attempt in escalation_e2e.json). On a scene, the stop comes at the first near-cap batch in row-major slice order, which can be most of a pass. The Walltime bullet suggests a resubmit makes progress. That holds only across attempts: an attempt has no checkpoint, so one that needs more than --time restarts from zero on every resubmit. None of this changes outputs; it changes cost and how the pilot interprets an OOM.
findings.suggested_fix: Restate it as: the retained-mask term stays put, the per-slice transient doubles with the cap, so later attempts can OOM. Drop 'usually in minutes'. Add: an attempt is all-or-nothing, so give a scene whose single pass exceeds 12 h a longer --time.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour:
The worst-case GPU mask memory is about 1 MiB x max_det x batch (retained uint8 masks, constant under escalation) plus about 5 MiB x max_det for the slice being processed. The second term comes from the float32 interpolate in process_mask plus the byte copy, and it doubles at every escalation step. Worst case, that transient is about 5.4, 10.7, 21.5 and 43 GiB at caps 1100, 2200, 4400 and 8800, so later attempts can OOM on cards below that.

A failed attempt runs until the first near-cap batch in slice order. On a scene that can be most of a pass, not minutes. Attempts are all-or-nothing, with no checkpoint inside an attempt. A scene whose single pass at the current (cap, batch) exceeds --time=12:00:00 needs a longer --time, because resubmitting will not finish it.

findings.title: Runbook commands are not runnable as written (DEST placeholder against the no-DEST decision, DTN loop without an environment, Progress command's variables)
findings.detail: (a) The §3 detect command passes DEST=<durable dir>. That contradicts the maintainer's 2026-10-15 choice recorded 30 lines later (transfer from $SCRATCH, no DEST), and if pasted, '<durable' is parsed as an input redirection. (b) The DTN fetch loop runs a bare 'python scripts/prep_pds_scene.py ... --out-root $SCENES'. It has no 'ml python/3.12.1', no venv activation and no cd $REPO, and $SCENES is only defined inside the sbatch scripts. (c) The Progress command uses $SCENES and $OUT, which also exist only inside the sbatch scripts. 'campaign.py status' builds a StageLedger per manifest row, and StageLedger.__init__ mkdirs, so a status run with unset variables creates a directory per row under the cwd and reports every scene as pending.
findings.suggested_fix: Drop DEST from the §3 command. Give the DTN loop and the Progress command the same preamble as the sbatch (ml; source $ENV_DIR/bin/activate; cd $REPO; export SCENES=... OUT=...). Make status read-only (do not construct StageLedger for a missing directory).

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: The §3 command should drop DEST, giving `--export=ALL,MANIFEST=$M,REPO=$REPO,ARMS=256`, to match the 2026-10-15 decision. The DTN loop and the Progress command need the sbatch preamble first: `ml python/3.12.1` or the module the sbatch uses, `source $ENV_DIR/bin/activate`, `cd $REPO`, and `export SCENES=$SCRATCH/campaign/scenes OUT=$SCRATCH/campaign/out` (plus M defined before line 51). With SCENES or OUT unset, the status command does not create directories; argparse rejects the missing option values. The mkdir side effect only happens when `--out` points somewhere: status then makes an empty `<out>/<ObsId>/` for every manifest row. Checking `Path(p['out_dir']).exists()` before building StageLedger would make status truly read-only.

findings.title: verify/status ignore the ledger's latest arm state: a stale ok:true handoff survives a failed re-run, and the handoff's 'attempts' mixes unrelated runs
findings.detail: status lets an existing handoff.json override the ledger. A scene re-run after a code change whose detection then fails (verify not reached) keeps the old ok:true handoff and shows 'verified'. A walltime kill mid-attempt shows 'prepped', because the latest entry is a 'running' marker. A standalone 'campaign.py verify' in that state passes the previous run's layer and manifest. verify also does not know the intended arm set, so leftover layers from a config-2 trial in the same OUT dir are listed and checksummed as part of a config-1 hand-off. _arm_attempts lists every finished entry of the stage regardless of base_key, i.e. across code versions, rasters or weights. After any re-run, the 'attempts behind each layer' sent to hirise2ctx can describe attempts that did not produce the delivered layer.
findings.suggested_fix: In verify, require the latest ledger entry of each arm stage to be COMPLETE, with artifacts matching the layer's digest. Take the expected arm set as an argument (detect knows it). Filter attempts to the delivered layer's base_key.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: status should take each arm stage's latest ledger state as authoritative: a later FAILED or "running" entry should override an older handoff.json, or the handoff should record the ledger state or digests it verified and be invalidated when they change. verify should require the latest ledger entry for each expected arm to be COMPLETE, with artifact digests equal to the layer's current sha256. It should take the expected arm set from detect's --arms and ignore or flag other layers. _arm_attempts should list only the attempts whose base_key matches the delivered layer's COMPLETE entry.

findings.title: Runbook step 0 is blocked: pack_for_cluster refuses the current tree because of an untracked evidence file
findings.detail: make_stamp counts every 'git status --porcelain' line, untracked files included. The code repo currently reports '?? data/review/stack_equivalence.json' (dated 2026-08-19; not ignored, because .gitignore:180 re-includes data/review/*.json). So 'pack_for_cluster.py --out ...' exits with 'refusing to pack a dirty tree'. The obvious workaround, --allow-dirty, stamps git_dirty: true and that path into CODE_STAMP. code_identity then copies git_dirty: true into every cluster manifest and handoff.json, over a file that is not even in the tarball. Separately, the tarball silently carries the ignored src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth.egg-info/ (harmless: it is outside the digested package).
findings.suggested_fix: Commit (or delete) data/review/stack_equivalence.json before packing. Optionally have make_stamp consider only paths inside the packed trees (src/, scripts/, sherlock/, pyproject.toml).

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: The finding describes the current behaviour correctly: as the tree stands, packing exits with "refusing to pack a dirty tree (1 paths, e.g. ['data/review/stack_equivalence.json'])". There are two ways to unblock it. One is to commit or delete data/review/stack_equivalence.json before packing. The other is to restrict make_stamp's dirty check to the packed paths (src/, scripts/, sherlock/, pyproject.toml), for example `git status --porcelain -- src scripts sherlock pyproject.toml`. Either way, CODE_STAMP stops reporting git_dirty: true for content the tarball does not contain.

findings.title: attempt_key's backward compatibility protects no existing ledger entry: the stage key embeds the package digest, which the escalation commit itself changed
findings.location: YOLOv8-BeyondEarth/scripts/run_multiscale_arms.py:184-196; src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth/runstate.py:230; docs/code_review_backlog.md 2026-10-14 handoff item 8; commit 49c97ae message
findings.detail: The docstring, the commit and backlog item 8 say batch_size is keyed only when it differs from 8, 'so no existing ledger entry is orphaned'. The formula is right: with the code held fixed, the key at batch 8 equals the old key, and the test pins that. But every stage_key includes code_source, the content digest of src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth. Commit 49c97ae edited predict.py (62 lines), so every entry written before it is STALE regardless. That includes the 2026-08-19 Sherlock HiRISE arm keys (e826eb4c..., 529bd1aa..., cc83bee0...). Those banked arms will recompute if run through this runner. It is harmless for the pilot, which uses new scenes, but anyone budgeting walltime on the claim would be wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Reword it to: compatible only with entries written by the same package code; the shim exists so a future escalation-only release does not orphan same-code ledgers.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: Keying batch_size only when it differs from 8 keeps a batch-8 key equal to the earlier formula only for entries written by byte-identical package code. Each stage key includes the src/YOLOv8BeyondEarth content digest, and 49c97ae itself edited predict.py, so every ledger entry written before 49c97ae is stale and recomputes. The commit-message and backlog item 8 wording should say the shim keeps future escalation-free releases with unchanged package code from orphaning same-code ledgers, not that no existing entry is orphaned.

findings.title: PDS prep has never run on the cluster's pip-wheel GDAL; the label route depends on its PDS and JPEG 2000 drivers
findings.detail: prepare_scene opens the .LBL and requires GDAL's PDS driver to follow COMPRESSED_FILE into the JP2, which needs a JPEG 2000 driver (JP2OpenJPEG or similar) in the wheel's bundled GDAL. The only conversions so far ran on the laptop's conda GDAL 3.10 (sidecar 'gdal': '3.10'). The cluster venv uses the rasterio 1.4.3 manylinux wheel, which was never asked to open a PDS label. The driver and frame checks make any mismatch loud: it refuses rather than writing a raster in another frame. Without a pre-check, though, a 62-task CPU array, and every aftercorr-dependent GPU task, can fail on the first night.
findings.suggested_fix: On a dev node, run prep_pds_scene.py --lbl on the already-fetched ESP_028537_2270 LBL+JP2 with --compare-to the laptop's (or Prieur's) raster. It must report IDENTICAL, with transform and CRS equal, before submitting the array.

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: Run one pre-flight conversion before submitting the prep array. Inside the cluster venv (or on a dev node), run `prep_pds_scene.py --lbl <ESP_028537_2270_RED.LBL> --compare-to <the laptop/Prieur raster>`. It should open with driver PDS and print IDENTICAL, and the sidecar should show frame_check dx/dy 0.0. Optionally, also add a driver probe to the env smoke test: `'PDS' in rasterio.drivers.raster_driver_extensions()` or `rasterio.Env().drivers()` containing PDS and JP2OpenJPEG. Failures already stop the run loudly rather than producing wrong output, so this is about not losing a night of cluster time, not about correctness.

findings.title: The 0.40 floor's effect on scene-to-scene level consistency is not reported, and the doubling of spread rests almost entirely on ESP_025650_2165
findings.location: docs/configuration_study_plan.md:146-161 (§The score floor is the lever) and :225-230 (D36)
findings.detail:
I reproduced every gap-finder number independently and extended the analysis to all 10 candidates (C1GS included), floors 0.10-0.50, 40/80 m cells, size floors 1.4105/2.0/3.0 m, and both tile subsets. hirise2ctx selects models on pooled Spearman and calibrates globally, so a label level that varies by scene goes straight into their map. The write-up never shows this axis.

On all 48 tiles at 40 m, C1's per-image area ratio (017355/025650/028537/037018) is 1.75/1.30/1.50/1.97 at 0.10 (log-SD 0.158, within-image tile bootstrap [0.098, 0.249]) and 1.04/0.48/1.01/0.73 at 0.40 (log-SD 0.312 [0.266, 0.420]). The paired bootstrap difference is +0.156 [+0.065, +0.253]. Held out, C1's max/min is 2.13 at 0.10 and 3.86 at 0.40.

The registered RMSE cannot see this. ESP_017355_2260 supplies 91.9% of C1@0.40's held-out squared error. ESP_025650_2165 (18 cells) supplies 1.5% and ESP_037018_2170 0.7%. Pooled label-vs-truth Spearman does not see it either: 0.922 at 0.10 against 0.923 at 0.40.

How much rests on the atypical images:
- Drop ESP_025650_2165, which fails v3's filters: the floor effect becomes +0.047 [-0.120, +0.214].
- Keep only the two v3-like images (017355 and 028537; both near-nadir, incidence 42 and 58 deg): C1@0.40 is the most consistent setting, 1.044 vs 1.011 (log-SD 0.016), against 0.078 at 0.10. The difference is -0.054 [-0.117, +0.024].
- At a 2.0 m size floor, which is fairer given the coarse images' human minimum diameters of 1.57/1.66 m: 0.274 [0.226, 0.375] at 0.40 against 0.182 at 0.10, difference +0.097 [-0.003, +0.204], marginal.

So it is a trade-off between level and consistency. On the images that resemble v3, the floor fixes the level without hurting consistency. On the two atypical images, one global floor roughly doubles a scene-level offset.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a per-image level table (C1 at 0.10/0.25/0.40, all tiles and held out, with the bootstrap log-SD) to §Results and to the D36 bullet. Say plainly: the 0.40 level calibration is established on ESP_017355_2260 and ESP_028537_2270, both ~1.0. On ESP_025650_2165 (fails v3's filters) and ESP_037018_2170 (resampled grid), one global floor turns a scene-level confidence offset into a level bias of about 2x. Neither RMSE nor pooled label-vs-truth Spearman detects that. Recommend that hirise2ctx monitor a per-scene confidence statistic in v3 (for example the median score of detections >= 3 m, or the fraction of them >= 0.40) to flag scenes where 0.40 will under-read.

findings.title: 'No {512,256} preset is needed' needs a qualifier: at matched floors C2 is more scene-consistent, entirely because the 256 arm under-detects on ESP_025650_2165
findings.detail:
On RMSE every candidate ties, so the registered result stands. On cross-scene consistency (all 48 tiles, 40 m), C2 production at its own RMSE-best floor of 0.40 reads 1.07/0.65/1.07/0.76 (log-SD 0.218 [0.178, 0.291]). C1 at 0.40 reads 0.312, a paired difference of +0.095 [+0.044, +0.168]. At 0.15, C2 reads 1.67/1.63/1.55/1.67 (log-SD 0.032 [0.019, 0.123]). The pattern persists at size floors of 2.0 m (C2@0.40 0.176 vs C1@0.40 0.274) and 3.0 m (0.123 vs 0.310).

All of it comes from ESP_025650_2165. Without that image, C1@0.40 minus C2@0.40 is 0.000 [-0.020, +0.033] at 1.41 m and -0.000 [-0.021, +0.033] at 2.0 m.

The mechanism is a scene-specific failure of the 256 arm, not a floor effect:
- In-ROM rows >= 1.41 m at 0.10: the 512 arm alone gives 1,155 rows on 025650 against the 256 arm's 819 (1.41x). On the other three images it gives 0.74-0.89x the 256 arm's count.
- C1's human recall at 0.10 is 0.66 on 025650 against 0.93/0.93/0.89, and it is low at every size: 0.54 / 0.75 / 0.76 for 1.4-2 / 2-3 / 3-5 m humans. C2 raises it to 0.77 / 0.93 / 0.97.
- C2's gain is the 481 kept 512-arm rows: median D 2.58 m, 74% of them 2-3 m, and only 27% with a centroid inside a human polygon at 0.10 (63% at 0.40). They add 76% of C1's area on 025650 at 0.10 (42% at 0.40), against 10-19% (2-6%) elsewhere.

So C2's consistency on this image is partly bought with unmatched area: its FP-area share is 1.11 against C1's 0.48. Its matched recall gain is real (0.33 -> 0.40 at 0.40). The 512 arm does nothing for ESP_037018_2170 (0.73 -> 0.76).
findings.suggested_fix: Qualify the bullet. 'No preset is needed' holds for scenes like ESP_017355_2260 and ESP_028537_2270, where the 512 arm adds 2-6% of area at 0.40. The campaign has no detector for such a scene, and v3's angle filters are the only protection. Report that the consistency advantage of C2 at matched floors is that one image.

findings.title: The mechanism behind 'one floor calibrates the average scene' is a scene-level confidence offset, and D36 understates which images are low
findings.detail:
The numbers in the write-up are correct. Held out at 0.40, C1 reads 1.088/0.307/1.187/0.901; on all tiles 1.044/0.482/1.011/0.732. The reason is not stated.

The low images are low because their real boulders score lower and fall below the floor. Mask size is not the cause:
- One-to-one centroid-in-polygon matches at 0.10 have median scores of 0.619/0.392/0.669/0.448, and the 0.40 floor keeps 79/49/83/60% of them. The unique <= 1 m match gives 0.628/0.393/0.671/0.449.
- It is not a size effect. For humans 3-5 m, the median matched score is 0.635/0.401/0.687/0.486.
- Recall at 0.40 is 0.74/0.33/0.77/0.53. The matched-mask/human area ratio is 1.13/1.11/1.04/1.26, so mask size is not what makes the two images low.
- On ESP_037018_2170, oversized TP masks partly offset the lost count.
- On ESP_025650_2165, a further 34% of humans are missed before any floor applies (recall 0.66 at 0.10).

Inconsistency: :161 says 'two of the four images come out low', but the D36 bullet at :228 says 'one image is 3x low at it'. ESP_037018_2170 is 0.73x on all tiles.

findings.title: ESP_025650_2165's Prieur raster uses a different 8-bit rule (round(DN*255/998)), not min((DN+2)>>2,255)
findings.detail:
I fetched the PDS RED JP2 next to its LBL (the LBL is byte-identical to data/pds_scenes's copy) and read it through GDAL's PDS driver. The transform, CRS and shape equal the Prieur raster, so the frames agree.

The radiometry does not match. Over the 10 ROM tiles (2.5 Mpx), pds_prep's rule matches only 0.15% of pixels: mean -2.75 DN, max |d| 5, larger on bright ground (-4.0 DN at mean 192). A least-squares fit gives Prieur = 0.25548*DN + 0.002 (residual SD 0.29). round(DN*255/998) reproduces 99.95% of pixels, a per-scene max stretch.

The ROM crops the detector saw are identical to the Prieur raster. So this image's detections were made on contrast stretched ~2.2% above a v3 pds_prep raster. That is another way it is unrepresentative of v3, though too small to explain on its own a confidence offset of 0.39 vs 0.67. pds_prep's pixel-for-pixel claim covers only 017355 and 028537, so the docs are not wrong.
findings.suggested_fix: Note it where ESP_025650_2165 is described as atypical. The image differs from v3 inputs in viewing geometry (incidence 37.8 deg, emission 25.2 deg) and in its 8-bit stretch (DN*255/998 vs (DN+2)>>2).

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: The Prieur ESP_025650_2165 raster is the PDS RED DN under a per-scene linear stretch, about round(DN*255/998). In my count that reproduces 98.6% of the ROM-tile pixels; the finder reported 99.95%, so the exact formula is slightly uncertain. pds_prep's (DN+2)>>2 matches 0.15% of pixels (mean -2.75 DN, max |d| 5). The georeferencing is identical to the label frame.

findings.title: ESP_037018_2170 passes v3's angle filters; only its resampled grid sets it apart, and that cause is untested
findings.detail:
The PDS label fetched into scratch gives INCIDENCE 53.19 deg, EMISSION 7.62 deg and MAP_SCALE 0.5 m/px EQUIRECTANGULAR. This image would pass v3's 40-70 deg / <15 deg filters.

The raster BoulderNet ran on is +proj=sinu, R=3396190, 0.59518 m/px, 13411x31045: a resampled MRDR, not a native RDR grid. Its ROM crops are identical to it.

So unlike ESP_025650_2165, its low level (0.73x all tiles at 0.40; matched median score 0.448; TP masks 1.27x human, the largest of the four) cannot be set aside on viewing geometry. Resampling softness is a plausible cause but has not been measured. If it is not the cause, v3 scenes could show the same low confidence.

Its truth also has nothing below 1.665 m (1st percentile 1.87 m). At 1.41 m its humans omit the 1.4-1.66 m population, and at 2.0 m its C1@0.40 level is unchanged (0.74).
findings.suggested_fix: When attributing the spread to 'atypical images', say that only ESP_025650_2165 is excluded by v3's filters. ESP_037018_2170 differs only in being resampled (0.595 m/px Sinusoidal from a 0.5 m/px RDR), and whether that causes its low confidence is unknown. Treat the 0.40 floor's transfer to v3 scenes as established on one 0.25 m/px image (ESP_028537_2270).

verdicts.correct_value_or_behaviour: Confirmed: INCIDENCE 53.19 deg, EMISSION 7.62 deg, label MAP_SCALE 0.5 m/px EQUIRECTANGULAR. The raster used is +proj=sinu, 0.59518 m/px, 13411x31045.
